questions.question: What are generics in TypeScript? Explain with examples.
questions.title: TypeScript Generics Explained — Functions, Classes & Constraints
questions.direct_answer:
What are generics in TypeScript? Explain with examples.

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the type checker, emit pipeline, and how types line up with runtime JS), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** Type parameters for functions/classes/interfaces, constraints via extends, default type parameters, type inference.

**Classic weak answer:** Using any instead of generics — you lose type information end-to-end; generics preserve relationships between inputs and outputs.

**Senior finish:** Show identity function, generic constraints with keyof, default type params, and inferring K from arguments.

sections.title: Why this question matters
sections.content:
This question — **TypeScript Generics Explained — Functions, Classes & Constraints** — shows up constantly in **frontend / fullstack** interviews because it separates candidates who memorized docs from candidates who can **reason about real systems**.

**Restate the prompt:** What are generics in TypeScript? Explain with examples.

A gold-level answer does four things in order:

1. **Define** the terms in plain English (what it is / what problem it solves).
2. **Explain the mechanism** (what runs when: browser, bundler, framework, network).
3. **Compare trade-offs** (speed vs correctness vs security vs DX) with **when you would not use** the default.
4. **Ground it in production** — caching, auth, observability, tests, or an incident you handled.

Interviewers are listening for: **Type parameters for functions/classes/interfaces, constraints via extends, default type parameters, type inference**.

The fastest way to lose points is: **Using any instead of generics — you lose type information end-to-end; generics preserve relationships between inputs and outputs**.

If you only add one “senior” layer, make it: **Show identity function, generic constraints with keyof, default type params, and inferring K from arguments**.

sections.title: Deep dive — what to say
sections.content:
### What to explain (middle of the answer)

- **Core mechanics:** Type parameters for functions/classes/interfaces, constraints via extends, default type parameters, type inference
- **Concrete shape:** give a small code or config snippet *only if it clarifies* (5–15 lines max).
- **Interviewer follow-ups:** expect “what breaks in production?”, “how do you debug?”, “what would you measure?” — answer them proactively.

### How to sound senior (without rambling)

- Tie the feature to **user-visible outcomes** (performance, accessibility, security).
- Mention **one failure mode** you have actually seen (race, stale cache, hydration mismatch, flaky test).
- Close with **one decision rule** (“choose X when …; choose Y when …”).

questions.question: How do generic constraints work in TypeScript? Explain extends and keyof.
questions.title: TypeScript Generic Constraints — extends, keyof & Mapped Types
questions.direct_answer:
How do generic constraints work in TypeScript? Explain extends and keyof.

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the type checker, emit pipeline, and how types line up with runtime JS), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** T extends U constraints, keyof T to pick property keys, K extends keyof T for strongly-typed property accessors.

**Classic weak answer:** Allowing T extends any — provides no constraint and defeats the purpose; use object, Record<string, unknown>, or a specific shape.

**Senior finish:** Write a strongly-typed getProp<T, K extends keyof T>(obj: T, key: K): T[K] and mention this pattern powers Formik/React Hook Form.

questions.question: What is the difference between generic functions and generic classes in TypeScript?
questions.title: Generic Functions vs Generic Classes in TypeScript — Differences
questions.direct_answer:
What is the difference between generic functions and generic classes in TypeScript?

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the type checker, emit pipeline, and how types line up with runtime JS), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** Function generics infer per call; class generics persist per instance; ergonomics and use cases differ.

**Classic weak answer:** Putting a type parameter on a class when only one method uses it — prefer a generic method instead.

**Senior finish:** Show a Cache<T> class vs a method-level generic; note React.Component<P, S> classic generic-class example.
